reconstructed_theorem_text: For every complete real inner-product normed spaces E and H, every map F:E->H and derivative assignment D:E->(E->L[R]H), assume F has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w in E. Let M1,M2 be supplied nonnegative real numbers. Assume norm_op(D(w))<=M1 whenever norm_E(w)<=1, and norm_op(D(w)-D(u))<=M2*norm_E(w-u) whenever both w and u have norm at most 1. Define V(r,w)=2*inner_product_H(r,F(w)) for r in H,w in E. Let A_w=(D(w)).adjoint:H->L[R]E be the actual Hilbert adjoint, and define G(r,w)=2 times (A_w(r)-inner_product_E(A_w(r),w) times w) for all r,w. Then the following three universally quantified conclusions hold. First, for every r in H and w in E, V(r,.) has full ambient Frechet derivative at w equal to the continuous real linear functional v->2*inner_product_E(A_w(r),v), equivalently v->2*inner_product_H(r,D(w)(v)); in Lean notation it is 2 times innerSL R (A_w(r)). Second, for every r in H and unit w in E, inner_product_E(w,G(r,w))=0; for every tangent vector v satisfying inner_product_E(w,v)=0, inner_product_E(G(r,w),v)=2*inner_product_H(r,D(w)(v)); and norm_E(G(r,w))<=2*M1*norm_H(r). Third, for every r,q in H and unit w,u in E, norm_E(G(r,w)-G(q,u))<=2*M1*norm_H(r-q)+2*(M2+2*M1)*norm_H(q)*norm_E(w-u). On a unit base point, the explicit G is the orthogonal projection of 2*(D(w)).adjoint(r) onto w-perpendicular and represents the restriction of the ambient derivative of V(r,.) to that tangent subspace. The same algebraic formula defines G at nonunit points, but the orthogonal-projection interpretation and the listed tangent and norm conclusions have the unit conditions shown. The parameter r is fixed when differentiating V(r,.). All differentiability and quantitative conditions on F,D,M1,M2 are supplied hypotheses, not conclusions or existentially selected constants. E,H may be infinite dimensional; both are explicitly complete. The final estimate has the displayed norm(q) dependence and does not assert a residual-independent global product Lipschitz constant. No measure, integral, polynomial, label, loss definition beyond the actual V formula, or finite-dimensional assumption is present.
objects: Complete real inner-product normed spaces E,H; supplied map F and its supplied derivative assignment D; nonnegative supplied constants M1,M2; scalar pairing function V; Hilbert adjoints A_w=(D(w)).adjoint; explicit vector field G; arbitrary coefficient vectors r,q in H; base points w,u and tangent test directions v in E.
domains: E,H have NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, and CompleteSpace structures, without a finite-dimensionality restriction. F:E->H; D:E->(E->L[R]H). Each adjoint A_w is a continuous real linear map H->E. V:H->E->R and G:H->E->E. M1,M2:R are nonnegative. Bounds on D and its operator differences use the closed ball norm<=1, whereas the projected-field conclusions and final estimate use exact unit base points. Vector norms are Hilbert norms and norms of continuous linear maps are operator norms. innerSL R z denotes the continuous linear functional v->inner_product_E(z,v).
quantifiers: For every pair E,H with the stated structures, F,D, and proof that HasFDerivAt(F,D(w),w) holds for every w, take any M1,M2 with M1>=0,M2>=0 satisfying the displayed uniform closed-unit-ball bounds. Define V,G once. The first conclusion quantifies every r:H,w:E with no unit condition. The second quantifies every r,w and assumes norm(w)=1, then gives orthogonality, a universal statement over every v perpendicular to w, and the norm bound. The third quantifies every r,q:H and w,u:E and assumes both base norms equal 1. There are no existential constants or derivative witnesses among the conclusions.
assumptions: F has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w. Both spaces are explicitly complete real inner-product normed spaces. M1,M2 are given nonnegative reals; norm_op(D(w))<=M1 holds for all w in the closed unit ball; and norm_op(D(w)-D(u))<=M2*norm_E(w-u) holds for every pair in that ball. These are supplied regularity and quantitative hypotheses. No differentiability of D, bound on F itself, finite dimensionality, positivity stronger than nonnegativity of M1,M2, or bounds on r,q are assumed.
conclusion: With V(r,w)=2*inner_product_H(r,F(w)) and G(r,w)=2 times ((D(w)).adjoint(r)-inner_product_E((D(w)).adjoint(r),w) times w): (1) for all r,w, V(r,.) has Frechet derivative 2*innerSL R ((D(w)).adjoint(r)) at w. (2) For every r and unit w, G(r,w) is perpendicular to w, pairs with each v perpendicular to w as inner_product_E(G(r,w),v)=2*inner_product_H(r,D(w)(v)), and has norm at most 2*M1*norm_H(r). (3) For all r,q and unit w,u, norm_E(G(r,w)-G(q,u))<=2*M1*norm_H(r-q)+2*(M2+2*M1)*norm_H(q)*norm_E(w-u).
scopes: The scalar derivative keeps r fixed and varies w through the full E, including arbitrary ambient increments. By the adjoint characterization, its value on v is exactly 2*inner_product_H(r,D(w)(v)). For norm(w)=1, the map z->z-inner_product_E(z,w) times w is the orthogonal projection onto w-perpendicular; hence G(r,w) is the tangential representative of that scalar derivative. Tangent vectors are exactly those v with inner_product_E(w,v)=0. The projection interpretation and G norm bounds are stated only at unit base points; the raw formula G exists everywhere. The closed-ball regularity assumptions include both interior and boundary points. In the final estimate the second term uses norm(q), with no unit or boundedness premise on r,q; its dependence is asymmetric exactly as displayed. Zero M1 or M2 is permitted. If E has no unit points, the unit-conditioned conclusions are vacuous while the scalar ambient derivative conclusion still applies. No manifold calculus identification beyond this explicit projection and tangent pairing is needed.
constant_dependencies: M1 and M2 are supplied constants controlling D on the fixed radius-1 closed ball. The ambient scalar derivative and G each have literal factor 2. The unit-point norm bound is exactly 2*M1*norm(r). The two-field bound has exact coefficients 2*M1 on norm(r-q) and 2*(M2+2*M1)*norm(q) on norm(w-u). These depend on the given M1,M2 and the displayed coefficient-vector norms; there is no unspecified factor, dimension dependence, or additional existential constant. The result does not replace the norm(q) factor by a constant independent of unbounded r,q.
